exam.title: Session 8 — Python Practice
exam.description: 40-question source-scoped practice for NumPy Fundamentals, Arrays & Vectorized Data Operations.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `NumPy ndarray` according to the taught session?

options.text: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.
`shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.
`np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

explanation.ar: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to create an efficient numerical array?

options.text: arr.shape
np.array(...)
np.zeros(shape) / np.ones(shape)
np.arange(start, stop, step)

explanation.ar: `np.array(...)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: create an efficient numerical array.

questions.question: Which structure does NumPy center around for numerical work?

options.text: Dictionary-only tables
File objects
N-dimensional arrays / ndarrays
Python sets

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `NumPy ndarray` behavior: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.

questions.question: A learner uses plain Python lists for a task that specifically needs the taught NumPy vectorized numerical operations. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `arr.shape` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `NumPy ndarray` has no rules.
Convert the task to `np.zeros()/np.ones()` without changing the logic.
Create a NumPy array and use NumPy operations when the course concept calls for array computing.

explanation.ar: Create a NumPy array and use NumPy operations when the course concept calls for array computing.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Array Shape` according to the taught session?

options.text: `shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.
`np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.
`np.linspace()` creates a requested number of evenly spaced values between two endpoints.

explanation.ar: `shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to inspect array dimensions?

options.text: np.zeros(shape) / np.ones(shape)
arr.shape
np.arange(start, stop, step)
np.linspace(start, stop, num)

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. `arr.shape` is the course-aligned choice for this task: inspect array dimensions.

questions.question: If a 2D array has 2 rows and 3 columns, what shape is taught?

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `Array Shape` behavior: `shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.

questions.question: A learner reads shape as the total element count rather than dimensions. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `np.zeros(shape) / np.ones(shape)` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `Array Shape` has no rules.
Convert the task to `np.arange()` without changing the logic.
Interpret shape as one size per dimension, e.g. rows and columns.

explanation.ar: Interpret shape as one size per dimension, e.g. rows and columns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `np.zeros()/np.ones()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

explanation.ar: `np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to initialize an array with zeros or ones?

options.text: np.arange(start, stop, step)
np.zeros(shape) / np.ones(shape)
np.linspace(start, stop, num)
np.random...

explanation.ar: `np.zeros(shape) / np.ones(shape)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: initialize an array with zeros or ones.

questions.question: What does `np.zeros((2,3))` create?

options.text: A list with two zeros
A 3×2 identity matrix
A 2×3 array filled with zeros
A random array

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `np.zeros()/np.ones()` behavior: `np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.

questions.question: A learner passes a scalar count when the goal is a 2D shape. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `np.arange(start, stop, step)` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `np.zeros()/np.ones()` has no rules.
Convert the task to `np.linspace()` without changing the logic.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `np.arange()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

explanation.ar: `np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to generate regularly stepped values?

options.text: np.linspace(start, stop, num)
np.arange(start, stop, step)
np.random...
arr[row, col] / arr[start:end]

explanation.ar: `np.arange(start, stop, step)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: generate regularly stepped values.

questions.question: What does `np.arange(0,10,2)` produce?

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `np.arange()` behavior: `np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

questions.question: A learner expects the stop value 10 to be included automatically. What correction best matches the course?

questions.question: Which statement best describes `np.linspace()` according to the taught session?

questions.question: What is the key distinction of `np.linspace(0,1,5)`?

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Random Arrays` according to the taught session?

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Indexing & Slicing` according to the taught session?
